$comment: Every fact about every day, stated once. Generators read it; tools/course/verify.py proves it.

days.title: Build an Onboarding Tracker REST API
days.summary: POST/GET, validation, H2, tested with Bruno
days.plain: We build a small web service from scratch that keeps a list of new joiners. You send it details, it stores them and gives them back. It's the shape of almost every service the team looks after.

days.title: Complete the Accounts CRUD API
days.tagline: Follows on from the Onboarding Tracker workshop
days.summary: `PUT`, `DELETE`, 404s, problem-detail errors
days.plain: We finish a service that keeps bank-style accounts: changing and deleting them, and giving clear, consistent error messages when something is asked for that doesn't exist or doesn't make sense.

failingOnStarter: 07 Missing account is a problem detail
08 Invalid create names every bad field
09 Deleting a missing account is a problem detail too

diagram.change: New: `@RestControllerAdvice` turns `AccountNotFoundException` and validation errors into problem details; `PUT` and `DELETE` arrive, with 404s
diagram.why: One error format for every endpoint

days.title: Code Review: Six Bugs
days.summary: a rushed pull request, symptom by symptom
days.plain: Someone rushed a change and it broke six things. We follow each symptom back to its cause, the way a developer investigates a bug report from users.

failingOnStarter: 01 Bug 1 and 4 - create a GBP account gives 201

days.title: Refactor Without Changing Behaviour
days.summary: constructor injection, layers, a response DTO
days.plain: We tidy the code's structure without changing what it does, and prove nothing changed. Tidy code is cheaper and safer to change later.

days.title: Unit Tests with JUnit 5, AssertJ and Mockito
days.tagline: Fast tests for logic and services
days.summary: JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito
days.plain: We write automatic checks (tests) that prove small pieces of the service work. They run in seconds and catch mistakes before anyone else sees them.

days.title: Testing the Web Layer and the Repository
days.summary: `@WebMvcTest`, `@DataJpaTest`
days.plain: We test bigger pieces: the part that answers web requests and the part that talks to the database. Each test checks one layer on its own.

days.title: Get a 2022 Service Running, and Audit It
days.summary: get Java 11 / Boot 2.7 running, and audit it
days.plain: We pick up an older service written in 2022 and get it running on a modern laptop. Then we write down what's old about it: the starting point for every upgrade.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: Read, Write and Migrate JUnit 4 Tests
days.summary: read, write and migrate its tests
days.plain: Older services often have older tests. We learn to read them, add one, and move them to the current testing tool so they keep running after upgrades.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: What Do We Ship? Lockfile, Scan, Trace
days.summary: lockfile, OSV scan, trace the CVEs (OWASP A03)
days.plain: Every service is built from other people's code (libraries). We list exactly which ones we ship and check them against public lists of known security problems.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: Patch What You Can, Decide the Rest
days.summary: version overrides and recorded decisions
days.plain: We fix the security problems we can by moving to safer library versions, and write down a reasoned decision for the ones we can't fix yet.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: Fix the Security Misconfigurations
days.summary: actuator, H2 console, secrets (OWASP A02)
days.plain: We close doors that were left open by mistake: admin pages anyone could reach, and a password written straight into the code.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

failingOnStarter: 02 Actuator menu needs a login (401 once fixed)
03 Env is hidden from anonymous callers (401 once fixed)
04 Env does not exist even with a login (404 once fixed)
07 H2 console is off (404 once fixed)

days.title: Upgrade to Spring Boot 3.5 and Java 17
days.summary: OpenRewrite, and what it misses
days.plain: We move the older service onto a supported version of its framework and Java, using a tool that does most of the edits, then fix what the tool misses.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: Re-scan After the Upgrade
days.tagline: Upgraded isn't the same as done
days.summary: upgraded isn't done
days.plain: We scan again after the upgrade. Upgrading removes some problems and can add new ones, so 'upgraded' isn't the same as 'done'.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.title: Upgrade the JDK from 17 to 21
days.tagline: Inspect first, then change one line
days.summary: inspect first, then upgrade
days.plain: We move the older service to a newer Java version. We check what it uses first, then change it, then prove it still works.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

diagram.box: the JDK under the whole app

days.title: Login and Roles for the Modern API
days.summary: Spring Security, deny by default, roles (OWASP A01)
days.plain: We add logins to the modern service, so only known people get in, and each person can only do what their role allows.

diagram.change: `SecurityConfig` with HTTP Basic, roles `CUSTOMER` / `TELLER`, deny by default
diagram.why: OWASP A01 Broken Access Control: roles

days.title: Whose Account Is It? Fixing an IDOR
days.summary: an IDOR and ownership checks (OWASP A01)
days.plain: We fix a common security hole where a logged-in customer could see someone else's account just by changing a number in the address.

failingOnStarter: 05 Creating an account needs a username (400)

diagram.change: An `Account.username` owner column and an ownership check in `AccountService.getVisibleTo` (someone else's account is a 404)

days.title: Find and Fix an Injection
days.summary: string-built JPQL and bound parameters (OWASP A05)
days.plain: We find and fix code that let a user's input be run as part of a database command, one of the oldest and most damaging security mistakes.

failingOnStarter: 02 A quote in the currency finds nothing

diagram.change: String-built JPQL in the service is replaced by a query method, `findByUsernameAndCurrency`

days.title: Store Passwords Properly
days.summary: salted, slow hashes (OWASP A04, A07)
days.plain: We stop storing passwords in a readable form, and store them the way the security standards require, so a leaked database doesn't leak passwords.

diagram.change: A `PasswordEncoder` bean: `{noop}` plain-text passwords become salted `{pbkdf2}` hashes

days.title: Log Security Events
days.summary: failed logins and refused lookups (OWASP A09)
days.plain: We make the service write down security-relevant events, such as failed logins and refused requests, so attacks can be spotted and investigated.

diagram.why: OWASP A09: attacks you can see

days.title: All or Nothing: Safe Transfers
days.summary: `@Transactional`, failing closed (OWASP A10)
days.plain: A transfer moves money out of one account and into another. We make sure it happens completely or not at all: never half.

failingOnStarter: 08 Ada's balance is still 1200 after the failed transfers

diagram.change: `POST /accounts/{id}/transfers`; `@Transactional` on `transfer`, with every check before any change

days.title: Two Transfers at Once
days.tagline: The lost update, and optimistic locking
days.summary: lost updates and optimistic locking
days.plain: When two transfers touch the same account at the same moment, one can silently overwrite the other. We make the service notice and refuse.

diagram.change: A [`@Version`](glossary.md#version) field: a stale write fails at commit instead of overwriting; `OptimisticLockingFailureException` → 409 `Concurrent update`

days.title: Idempotent Payments
days.tagline: A retry must never pay twice
days.summary: a retry must never pay twice
days.plain: If a payment request is sent twice (say, the network dropped and the app retried), the customer must only be charged once. We make that guaranteed.

failingOnStarter: 04 Ada's balance went down by 50 once
05 Same key with a different amount is 422
11 Ada's balance went down again (an independent payment)

diagram.change: An [`Idempotency-Key`](glossary.md#idempotency-key) header, stored in the same transaction as the transfer: a retry replays the answer, a reused key with a different body is 422

days.title: Money Done Right
days.summary: currencies and decimal places
days.plain: Money has rules: different currencies, and a fixed number of decimal places. We stop the service rounding pennies away or mixing currencies.

failingOnStarter: 02 Pounds to Grace's dollar account is 400

diagram.change: A `Money` record (amount + [currency](glossary.md#iso-4217)) that refuses mixed currencies and never rounds silently ([rounding mode](glossary.md#rounding-mode) `UNNECESSARY`); `@Digits` allows 2 decimal places

days.title: Mask What You Show
days.tagline: Account numbers in responses and logs
days.summary: account numbers in responses and logs
days.plain: We hide most of each account number in what the service shows and records, so a screenshot or a log file can't leak a customer's full details.

failingOnStarter: 01 Ada sees her account number masked
02 Grace sees her account number masked
03 The teller's list is masked too
04 Teller opens a GBP account for Grace

diagram.change: One `Mask.accountNumber` helper: `****5678` in every response and log line; the stored number is unchanged

days.title: Maven for Gradle Users
days.tagline: Take a dependency finding through Maven
days.summary: `./mvnw dependency:tree`, a `<properties>` version override
days.plain: Many services are built with a tool called Maven rather than the Gradle we've used so far. Today we take the API we know from Day 5, now built with Maven, and do one common job with it: a ticket says one library must move to a newer patch version, so we make the change, prove it took effect, and keep everything working.

glance.apiClient: None today (a build day; Day 5's collection still works)

diagram.box: the build (`pom.xml`): Maven instead of Gradle

days.title: From Java 8 to 11
days.summary: move a Java 8 service to 11, and add JAXB back as a library
days.plain: Some of the team's services still run on Java 8, a version from 2014 that's long past its prime. Today we move one of them to Java 11. The move breaks the service, because Java 11 removed a built-in piece it relied on for producing XML files, so we add that piece back as a separate library and prove everything works again.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

diagram.box: the JDK under a small export service, and its XML library

days.title: Triage a Scanner Report
days.tagline: Every finding gets a fix or a recorded decision
days.summary: a SARIF report: fix, false positive, accept risk, duplicate
days.plain: The organisation's security scanner has checked our code and sent a list of possible problems. Some are real and we fix them; some are mistakes by the tool; one is real but we choose to live with it for now. Today we decide for each one, and write down why.

diagram.change: The notifications API key comes from configuration (`notifications.api-key`), not the code; API tokens are hashed with SHA-256, not MD5
diagram.why: [SAST](glossary.md#sast) findings triaged: fix, [false positive](glossary.md#false-positive) or [accepted risk](glossary.md#accepted-risk)

days.title: Zero-Day Drill
days.tagline: A critical CVE lands: find it, patch it, prove it, report it
days.summary: Log4Shell across a multi-project build: `dependencyInsight`, one version, evidence
days.plain: A serious security hole has been announced in a logging library that thousands of programs use. We have hours, not weeks, to find out which of our services contain it, update them, prove the update worked and report back. Today is a practice run of that emergency.

glance.build: Gradle 9.8 multi-project build: three services, two shared libraries (use the wrapper)

days.startsFrom: A new multi-project Gradle build: three services and two shared libraries

diagram.box: the libraries under every service, across the estate

days.title: Patch the Container, Not Just the Code
days.tagline: The base image is part of what we ship
days.summary: a supported, matching, non-root base image
days.plain: Our service doesn't run on its own: it ships inside a container image, which also holds a Java runtime and a small operating system. Those parts get security fixes too, and many findings in a scan are there, not in our code. Today we make the image use a supported, up-to-date base, the same Java version as the app, and an ordinary user instead of the all-powerful "root".

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs); Docker optional

diagram.box: the container image around the whole app

days.title: The Next Hop: Spring Boot 4 on Java 25
days.tagline: Upgrade one step at a time, and log every error
days.plain: The old service now runs on a version of its main framework that no longer gets free security fixes. The team's newer services already run on the next big release of that framework (version 4) and the latest Java. Today we move the old service up to match. We do it one step at a time and write down every error we hit, because the list of errors and fixes is what the next team will need.

days.title: Move a Pre-Boot Spring App onto Spring Boot
days.tagline: From XML and a WAR to @SpringBootApplication
days.summary: XML beans, `web.xml` and a WAR → Spring Boot 2.7 with embedded Tomcat
days.plain: Some of our older services were built with Spring before Spring Boot existed. They're wired together with XML files and have to be installed on a separate application server, which makes them slow to change and hard to upgrade. Today we move one onto Spring Boot, so it starts on its own and can follow the same upgrade path as our other services.

glance.build: Gradle 8.14 (use the wrapper; it downloads the JDKs)

days.startsFrom: A new pre-Boot Spring MVC codebase (WAR)

diagram.box: the whole (pre-Boot) app's wiring and packaging
